abstract: Thyroid hormones (TH) are essential for fetal development. We hypothesized that malaria in pregnancy (MiP) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge would disrupt the expression of placental TH transporters. Pregnant dams were infected with Plasmodium berghei ANKA at gestational day (GD) 13.5 or challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at GD17.5. Maternal thyroid parameters, fetal outcomes, placental inflammatory markers, TH transporters and deiodinases expression were assessed at GD18.5. Both MiP and LPS increased maternal serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and reduced fetal weight, whereas MiP decreased free thyroxine (fT4). MiP reduced fetal size and the fetal-to-placental weight ratio. Placental Cxcl1 mRNA increased in both sexes following MiP and in females following LPS injection, whereas Ccl2 mRNA increased only in males following LPS challenge. MiP reduced Slc7a8 mRNA in both sexes and Dio2 mRNA in males. No other significant changes in the assessed placental transcripts were detected in either model. At the protein level, MiP increased MCT8 immunostaining in the labyrinth zone (Lz) in both sexes and in the junctional zone (Jz) in males. MCT10 immunostaining decreased in the Lz and increased in the Jz in both sexes following both challenges. MiP increased LAT2 and OATP4A1 immunostaining in both zones in males. Following LPS challenge, MCT8 immunostaining increased in both zones in males, LAT2 increased in the Lz in males, and OATP4A1 increased in the Lz in both sexes. In conclusion, MiP and LPS-challenge disturb maternal thyroid and reshape placental TH transporter expression in a sex- and zone-dependent manner.
